introduction_markdown: CAMEROON GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination, June 2020, Ordinary Level, Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL QUESTIONS IN SECTION A and ANY TWO QUESTIONS FROM EITHER SECTION B or SECTION C. IN SECTIONS B AND C, ALL QUESTIONS CARRY EQUAL MARKS. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C but NOT a combination of all three. Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory, answer all questions). Section B: Mechanics (if this section is chosen, then Section C may not be chosen; answer any two questions). Section C: Statistics and Probability (if this section is chosen, then Section B may not be chosen; answer any two questions). All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators may be used. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2. Formulae Booklets may be used.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) The rate of change of the volume of a sphere is $48\pi\,\text{cm}^3\text{s}^{-1}$ at the instant when the radius is 6 cm.

Find:

(a) the rate of change of the radius of the sphere. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
With $V=\dfrac43\pi r^3$, $\dfrac{dV}{dr}=4\pi r^2$. By the chain rule

$$\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{dV}{dr}\cdot\frac{dr}{dt}\ \Longrightarrow\ 48\pi=4\pi(6)^2\,\frac{dr}{dt}=144\pi\,\frac{dr}{dt}.$$

$$\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac{48\pi}{144\pi}=\frac13.$$

**The radius is increasing at $\dfrac13\,\text{cm s}^{-1}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) the rate of change of the surface area of the sphere.

[The volume of a sphere, $V=\dfrac43\pi r^3$ and the surface area of a sphere, $A=4\pi r^2$] *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
With $A=4\pi r^2$, $\dfrac{dA}{dr}=8\pi r$. By the chain rule, at $r=6$ and $\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac13$:

$$\frac{dA}{dt}=\frac{dA}{dr}\cdot\frac{dr}{dt}=8\pi(6)\cdot\frac13=16\pi\approx50.3.$$

**The surface area is increasing at $16\pi\approx50.3\,\text{cm}^2\text{s}^{-1}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii) The area bounded by the curve $y^2=x^2$, the $x$-axis and the ordinates $x=0$ and $x=2$ is rotated completely about the $x$-axis. Find volume of the solid generated. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The volume of revolution about the $x$-axis between $x=a$ and $x=b$ is $V=\pi\int_a^b y^2\,dx$. Here the curve gives $y^2=x^2$ directly (it is the pair of lines $y=\pm x$; the part above the $x$-axis, $y=x$, bounds the area, and the part below gives the same solid):

$$V=\pi\int_0^2x^2\,dx=\pi\left[\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^2=\pi\cdot\frac83.$$

**The volume of the solid is $\dfrac{8\pi}{3}\approx8.38$ cubic units** (a cone of radius $2$ and height $2$: $\frac13\pi(2)^2(2)=\frac{8\pi}{3}$, which confirms the result).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(iii) The position vector of the centre of gravity of three particles of mass $m\,\text{kg}$, $n\,\text{kg}$ and $7\,\text{kg}$ which are at the points with position vectors $\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}$, $\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j}$ and $2\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j}$ respectively is $\dfrac32\mathbf{i}$.

Given that $m$ and $n$ are constants, find the values of $m$ and $n$. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The position vector of the centre of gravity is the weighted mean of the position vectors:

$$\bar{\mathbf{r}}=\frac{m(\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})+n(\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j})+7(2\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j})}{m+n+7}=\frac{(m+n+14)\mathbf{i}+(-2m+5n-21)\mathbf{j}}{m+n+7}.$$

This equals $\dfrac32\mathbf{i}$, so compare the components.

$\mathbf{j}$ component (zero): $-2m+5n-21=0$. (1)

$\mathbf{i}$ component: $\dfrac{m+n+14}{m+n+7}=\dfrac32\ \Longrightarrow\ 2(m+n+14)=3(m+n+7)\ \Longrightarrow\ m+n=7$. (2)

From (2), $n=7-m$. Put into (1): $-2m+5(7-m)-21=0\ \Longrightarrow\ 14-7m=0\ \Longrightarrow\ m=2$, then $n=5$.

Check: total mass $=2+5+7=14$; $\mathbf{i}$: $(2+5+14)/14=\frac{21}{14}=\frac32$ and $\mathbf{j}$: $(-4+25-21)/14=0$.

**$m=2$ and $n=5$.**
